title: Two private gardens in western Mass. open to the public for one day only - NewsBreak
text: HOLYOKE, Mass. (WWLP) – Two private gardens will open to the public for one day only this weekend as part of the Garden Conservancy’s Open Days program. On Saturday, August 16, visitors can explore Rock Valley Paradise in Holyoke and Thayer Garden in Hadley, offering a rare look at two distinctly different approaches to gardening and the opportunity to meet the gardeners behind them. Rock Valley Paradise in Holyoke serves as both a sanctuary and a working homestead for its owner, with the primary focus on growing food for the family. The quarter-acre garden includes a small orchard with 15 fruit trees—apples, peaches, plums, pears, apricots, and cherries—as well as berries, grapes, tomatoes, cucumbers, peppers, squash, eggplant, and other vegetables. The property also has two dairy goats, a dozen chickens, and two beehives. Thayer Garden in Hadley, set around a 1747 farmhouse and 1884 barn, has been cultivated by its owner for 32 years. The two-acre property features historic plantings of phlox, iris, daylilies, peonies, lilacs, and wisteria, along with newer additions such as a fishpond, shade garden, vegetable beds, and native pollinator plants. Scenic views include Mount Holyoke to the east and Connecticut River farmland to the west. The gardens will be open from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. to registered guests. Tickets are $10 per person or $5 for Garden Conservancy members. Children 12 and under are admitted free with a parent or guardian. No pets are allowed. Registration is available only through the Garden Conservancy’s website. The Garden Conservancy’s Open Days program, now in its 30th year, has welcomed more than 1.4 million visitors to thousands of private gardens across 41 states, ranging from urban rooftops to organic farms and historic estates.
